body.objective: Extract the compact-Gauss mechanism into a structural theorem for finitely many smooth charged clock/modulus fields on closed S3, separating vanishing total gauge charge from the possible survival of gauge-invariant relative-phase clocks.
body.stop_condition: Import the one-field separated scale/U1 theorem, the terminal two-field preflight and its conditional full-gate disposition.  If the two-field theory already passes the full physical gate, close this no-go/generalization task as NOT_ACTIVATED.  Otherwise formulate the most general finite set of smooth homogeneous complex scalars with integer compact-U1 charges, positive or declared-indefinite kinetic matrix, gauge-invariant potential and smooth Abelian connection on closed S3 within the declared two-derivative class.  Derive the integrated Gauss constraint and classify the charge-lattice kernel exactly by Smith normal form.  Prove necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions for nonzero individual phase velocities at zero total gauge charge, identify the dimension of the gauge-invariant relative-phase space, and derive its reduced kinetic form and raw-D/K_Berger moment map.  Determine whether positivity permits a nontrivial relative clock or whether an additional sign/source/boundary assumption is necessary.  Give explicit two-field witnesses or exact separators and state how boundaries or charged external sources change the theorem.
body.current_gate: closed-universe compact-Gauss and relative-clock structure theorem
body.forbid: no one-field Gauss no-go generalized to many fields without charge-lattice reduction; no total charge zero interpreted as all individual velocities zero; no indefinite cancellation called healthy; no boundary flux silently used on closed S3; no claim about nonhomogeneous or higher-derivative theories beyond the stated assumptions
activates: a justified charged-source/boundary-sector test or a surviving neutral relative-clock construction
body.resource_hint: STRUCTURAL GENERALIZATION.  Use Forge SNF, exact linear algebra and semialgebraic sign stratification as independent rails; keep the theorem finite-field and two-derivative scoped.
notes: This task prevents repeated one-model Gauss calculations and decides whether extra charged moduli are a credible mechanism before another large BV build.
